author: smimon
text:
IF - a quick question if you don't mind.

Are you finding that there are just more and more FOs happening? The
amount it is happening seems to just be increasing week by week.

I found RTM in October last year, and even though I am now relatively
experienced in chart reading, I am finding reading engulfs to be more
and more unreliable.

It's just not a minor problem either really - one of the main factors
for determining the next likely move on a chart is inferred by the
engulfs that are in play.

Many times, I have seen price react to a valid HTF important FL,
"engulf" the nearest opposing significant LTF FL - and then just turn in
 thin air and continue the move, and break through the HTF FL. Sure, if
you look back in chart history you will find some sort of swap - but
then you can do this ultimately for every single minor turn in the
market, and it's not exactly something you can predict.

It's making life extremely difficult - you don't know what you can
believe, and what you cannot. The best clue I have for whether it was a
real engulf or not, is how price behave afterwards.

author: Ifmyante
text:
You're right.

They have gotten much more devious over the last year.

They're playing the same game with the same rules, but they're making it
 much more difficult to know how far price is going to move.

With more and more people learning the basics of price reading, this is only to be expected.

Sure, it makes our life more difficult, but we've found ways to profit from it regardless

author: Art
text:
Question was addressed to IF but I hope MW you don't mind me jumping in.

Markets are interconnected.

If interest rates change for USD ir does affect Google. in 2 ways. If
rates rise it is more expensive for businesses to borrow money hence
fund their operations. Another thing if USD drop so EURUSD rate rises..
 that means for every Euro you will get more dollars. Hence the European
 traders get more value for their money due to exchange rate. So it does
 effect the local USD stock.

IF USD rates rise people want to allocate more money to dollar so they
get their interest. Hence more money inflow to US. probably more trades
in US markets.

But what I haven't figured out is this if we have let's say AUDJPY,
AUDUSD, AUDEUR, AUDNZD etc... then it becomes pretty complex to know
where i.e. the buying is coming from. If you have a short pop ready on
AUDJPY.... but everyone buys AUDUSD, AUDEUR, AUDNZD etc... will it then
not push the market through short setup on AUDJPY?

Probably I overthink .. as always

author: scoobydoo
text:
Art, in days gone by I had a go at trying to arbitrage between 3
pairs. I'd watch EURUSD, GBPUSD and GBPEUR. GBPEUR should technically be
 EURUSD divided by GBPUSD. If I saw that there was a discrepancy between
 this calculation and the actual GBPEUR quote I'd place trades on all
three with an aim to the gap closing, and being supposedly market
neutral at the same time.

Why I stopped? It didn't take long to realise the cost of trading this
way....it's a margin eater for one. Then u've got 3 sets of spread, then
 the overall profit is a very small number of pips...so positions have
to be huge to make it worthwhile.

I think nowadays it's virtually impossible for a small trader to do this
 as Triangular Arbitrage is probably handled by mega computers that keep
 the pairs in sync so quick.

Anyway, sorry IF for blabbering away on yer journal
